title: Invoice PDF export
brief:
Invoice PDF export

Customers ask for a downloadable invoice from the billing page

tasks.title: Invoice PDF route (server)
tasks.description:
## What
Add `GET /api/invoices/:id/pdf`, which returns one of the signed-in user's invoices as a PDF. This is the server half of invoice PDF export. A follow-up task builds the billing page and its Download button on top of this route.

## Why
Customers keep asking for a downloadable invoice from the billing page (brief #69). The server side is split out so it can be reviewed by itself.

## Scope
- Add the route in `server/routes.ts`. Use the same auth and `checkRateLimit(req.user.sub, 'read')` checks as `GET /invoices`. Task #4 (Extract auth middleware) is in progress. If its middleware is on main when you start, use it. Otherwise copy the inline token/verifyJwt pattern the other routes use.
- Look the invoice up only within `listInvoices(req.user.sub)`. An id that belongs to another user must get the same 404 as an unknown id, so fall through with `next()` as `/subscriptions/:id/cancel` does. This ownership check is the security property that matters most here.
- Respond with `Content-Type: application/pdf` and `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="invoice-<id>.pdf"`.
- PDF content: invoice id, issue date, amount formatted from `amountCents`, paid/unpaid status, and the customer's email and plan. Add small helpers in `server/store.ts` to look these up by user id. Line items, addresses, tax and branding are out of scope.
- Choosing how to generate the PDF is a Planning decision: a small dependency such as `pdfkit`, or a minimal hand-written PDF. Keep it light, and make it work under `node --experimental-strip-types`.
- Add tests for the route under `tests/` (vitest). supertest isn't installed, so choose between adding it and calling the handler directly. Task #7 owns the broader billing integration tests, so test only this route.
- No frontend changes. Those belong to the follow-up billing page task.

## Done when
- No or invalid token → 401.
- Another user's invoice id or an unknown id → 404.
- Your own invoice → 200, `application/pdf`, attachment filename `invoice-<id>.pdf`, body starts with `%PDF-`.
- Over the read rate limit → 429.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass.

tasks.title: Billing page invoice downloads (client)
tasks.description:
## What
Add an invoices section to the billing page with a Download PDF button for each invoice. The buttons call `GET /api/invoices/:id/pdf`, which the server task merged before this one started.

## Why
Customers keep asking for a downloadable invoice from the billing page (brief #69). This is the client half, reviewed separately from the server route.

## Scope
- Add a new `apiDownload(path, token)` (or similar) helper in `src/lib/http-client.ts`. It fetches with an `Authorization: Bearer` header, reads the response as a blob, and triggers the save through an object URL, using the filename from `Content-Disposition` or `invoice-<id>.pdf`. Don't change `apiFetch`, because task #5 (Generate API client types) is rewriting it.
- There is no billing page yet. `src/App.tsx` only lists subscriptions. Add a minimal invoices section that lists the user's invoices from `GET /api/invoices` (date, amount, paid) with a Download PDF button on each. Task #8 (Onboarding empty states) also touches billing pages. If a billing page from #8 is on main by then, build on it instead of creating a second one.
- The frontend sends no auth token today. The login flow is task #1 and out of scope here. Have the helper take a token parameter and wire it the way the rest of the app gets one, or leave a clear TODO if no token source exists yet.
- Show a simple error if a download fails. Don't change the server route.

## Done when
- The invoices section renders the user's invoices.
- Download PDF fetches the route with the token and saves `invoice-<id>.pdf`.
- A failed download shows an error and doesn't crash the page.
- `apiFetch` is unchanged.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.
